scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: I'm on the IT department head's machine (it_hod) and
I suddenly cannot reach any of the CS department computers (the 192.168.2.x
ones) -- every one of them just times out for me. My own department's
machines are fine, so this machine is not the problem: whatever joins the
departments together is. That is your side, not mine. It worked before and
it does not work now. Take a look and sort it out today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A thorough layer-by-layer investigation of the path between the IT LAN (192.168.1.0/24) and the CS LAN (192.168.2.0/24) reveals no fault anywhere in the network. The user's complaint does not correspond to an actual network anomaly.

Specifically: both subnets are directly connected to router0 (eth0 = 192.168.1.1/24 for IT, eth1 = 192.168.2.1/24 for CS); both interfaces are UP with correct addresses. IP forwarding is enabled on router0 and no iptables rules exist on router0, it_hod, or any CS host. All five CS hosts (192.168.2.2 through 192.168.2.6) respond to ICMP with 0% packet loss from it_hod, and the reverse path (cs_hod pinging 192.168.1.2) is equally clean. A traceroute from it_hod to cs_hod (192.168.2.2) shows exactly the expected two hops: router0 then the destination. At the L2 level, switch1's bridge (br0) has both eth0 (link to router0) and eth1 (CS LAN) up and bridged. The RIP daemon on router0 is running with configuration intact and has correctly converged; router1 and router2 both hold valid RIP-learned entries for 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24.

The user's report appears to be a false premise — either a transient glitch that self-resolved before investigation began (which is inconsistent with the lab's persistent-fault design), or a mistaken belief that connectivity was broken. No corrective action is needed; the network is fully operational.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states router0's IT/CS interfaces are UP with correct addresses and confirms inter-department routing by successful pings/traceroutes and RIP convergence, so it meets the axis.
